intro_html: Oyakodon is Japan's great weeknight bowl: chicken thighs and eggs simmered together in a sweet soy and mirin broth, spooned over rice so the sauce soaks in. Two proteins in one pot pushes each bowl to 47 grams of protein for about $1.84. Humble ingredients, restaurant results.
cost_closing_html: About $1.84 a bowl for a donburi that Japanese restaurants serve for $13. The chicken-and-egg combo is one of the cheapest high-protein pairings in the entire grocery store, and this dish was built around it.
shop_smart: Boneless skinless thighs at about $2.48 a pound beat breast on price and are the traditional cut here anyway. The right choice is also the cheap one for once.
Eggs do heavy protein lifting at roughly 12 cents each by the dozen. When eggs go on sale, this recipe should move to the top of your list.
Mirin is the one specialty buy. One bottle covers this batch with plenty left, and a splash of it upgrades stir fry sauce and teriyaki for months.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: 7 cups dry with water per your usual method.
In your big pot, combine the chicken broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken thighs cut into bite-size pieces and most of the green onions. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken reads 165 F.
Beat the eggs lightly, just until streaky, not uniform.
Pour the eggs evenly over the simmering chicken, cover, and cook 2 to 3 minutes. For meal prep that reheats safely, cook the eggs fully set, not runny.
Spoon the chicken and egg mixture with plenty of broth over rice in each container and top with the remaining green onions.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14, then ladle that weight over even scoops of rice. Every bowl lands at 724 calories and 47 grams of protein.

steps: Simmer broth, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar, then add bite-size chicken thighs and green onions.
Cook 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 165 F.
Pour lightly beaten eggs over the top, cover, and cook until fully set.
Spoon chicken, egg, and broth over rice in 14 containers and top with green onions.
